subject: general
question: A man on the top of a vertical tower observes a car moving at a uniform speed coming directly towards it. If it takes 10 minutes for the angle of depression to change from 45° to 60°, in how much total time will the car reach the tower?
solution:
**Given:**

The car takes 10 min for the angle of depression to change from 45° to 60°

**Concept used:**

tanθ = P/B

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/94e7340f2c47ba07e5da1d19152ecc63db883ae073c2e23fdca611ca147b7b52.png] 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/647a7f74309bbd8fd9b1e1beeb36c59481562658131db25895056bae15e5eefd.png] 

In ΔABC,

AB/BC = tan60°

⇒ h/x = √3

⇒ h = √3x ----(i)

In ΔABD,

AB/BD = tan45°

⇒ [h/(x + y)] = 1 

⇒ h = x + y ----(ii)

Comparing eq (i) & (ii) we get

√3x = x + y

⇒ √3x - x = y

⇒ (√3 − 1)x = y

Car covers the distance y in 10 min

So, (√3 − 1)x distance is covered in 10 min

So, x distance will be covered in 10/(√3 - 1) min

(10)/(√3 - 1) times (√3 + 1)/(√3 + 1)

⇒ (10(√3 + 1))/((√3)² - 1²)

⇒ (10(√3 + 1))/(3 - 1)

⇒ (10(√3 + 1))/(2)

⇒ 5(√3 + 1) min

⇒ (5√3 + 5) min

So, total time = 5√3 + 5 + 10

⇒ 15 + 5√3 min

**∴ The car will reach the tower in (15 + 5√3) minutes.**
